sn.c: The auditorium is deep and narrow, so the back Orchestra rows (P to R) can feel quite far from the stage despite the small house.
sn.sh: Back rows feel far back in this deep, narrow room

sn.c: Mezzanine seats are tight, and so is the legroom.
sn.sh: Mezzanine seats and legroom are tight

sn.c: Row A in the middle section of the Mezzanine gives a raised, very clear view of the stage.
The back rows of the Mezzanine are the least liked in this theater, but their views still beat similar seats in bigger Broadway houses.
For extra legroom in the Orchestra, pick row A or an aisle seat.

vs.sum: One of Broadway's smallest houses (597 seats) and one of its newest, built in 2015 as Second Stage's permanent home. The intimate scale means excellent sightlines from nearly every seat, though the modern design prioritizes function over grandeur.

acc.note: Elevator from lower lobby to Mezzanine. LOOP system for t-coils and cochlear implants.
